1.explanation:
1. components/prism-gcode.js (new): implements the G-code syntax definition using Prism.languages.gcode (or Prism.languages.reprap_gcode) with regex patterns for comments, G/M commands, and properties (X/Y/Z/E/etc).  
2. components/prism-gcode.min.js (new): the minified counterpart so that users can load the compressed version alongside other languages.  
3. components/index.js (modified): the central registry of all language components. You must add an entry for “gcode” so that the build system knows to include your new files and make the language available to Prism.  
4. examples.js (modified): the demo page script that populates the language dropdown and example snippets. Adding “gcode” here lets users select “G-code” in the live preview and see the highlighting in action.
1.bug_scenario: Prism currently doesn’t recognize or highlight G-code at all. In the screenshot you can see a small G-code program (with commands like ‘G28’, parameters like ‘X0’, and comments beginning with ‘;’) being rendered as plain text—no colors for comments, keywords or parameters. The user wants to add a new language identifier `gcode` so that comments, G/M-commands, and coordinate letters are all highlighted.

2.explanation: 1. components/prism-gcode.js & prism-gcode.min.js: These files need to be created to define the new language grammar under the identifier “gcode” (or alias to reprap_gcode). They will contain the RegExp rules for comments, G/M keywords, and properties as provided. Without them, Prism has no knowledge of G-code syntax. 2. components/index.js: This index lists all available language components to be bundled by the build. We must import or reference the new prism-gcode.js here so that the `gcode` language is registered in the final Prism.js build. Without updating the index, the new file would never be included or exposed to users.
2.bug_scenario: The user is requesting syntax highlighting support for G-code (commonly used in CNC/3D-printer code) in Prism.js. In the screenshot, lines starting with M and G commands (e.g. “G28”, “M190”) are displayed as plain text rather than colored tokens. They expect tokenization of comments (;…), keywords like G- and M-codes, and coordinate/property letters (X, Y, Z, etc.). Currently there is no `prism-gcode.js` in the components folder nor any registration in the language index, so Prism fails to recognize or highlight `gcode`.
